findings.title: Raw-HTML image sanitizer only matches double-quoted src, so other forms get through
findings.body: The regex only matches `src="..."` and stops at the first `>`. These forms are never matched and keep their original `src`: - `` (single quotes) - `` (no quotes) - `` (a `>` inside an earlier attribute) The PR says `data:` images are resolved inside WebView2 and never reach the resource filter. So with the setting ON, a `data:` image in any of these forms renders, even though the stated model says `data:` is always blocked. Any other scheme in these forms also skips the validation. I can't see `MarkdownPreviewHandlerControl.cs`, which might sanitize again later. Fix: parse the HTML instead of using a regex, or at least handle single-quoted and unquoted values and quoted `>`. If no match is found, drop the `` rather than leave it unchanged.

findings.title: Image files are read synchronously, with no size limit, on the WebView2 event thread.
findings.body: `File.Exists` and `File.ReadAllBytes` run inside `WebResourceRequested`, which fires on the UI thread. A slow or unreachable network share therefore freezes the preview pane. A large file under the allowed folder is read fully into memory. Any file type is served, not only images, so a link to a multi-GB file could do this. Files over 2 GB throw `IOException` and are blocked. Smaller but very large files can throw `OutOfMemoryException`, which is not caught here and can bring down the preview host. Fix: allow only known image extensions, cap the file size, and serve a `FileStream` through `e.GetDeferral()` instead of reading the whole file on the UI thread.

findings.title: Settings read errors other than FileNotFoundException break the whole preview.
findings.body: Only `FileNotFoundException` is caught. Other errors propagate: a malformed settings.json (`JsonException`), a sharing violation while the Settings UI is writing the file (`IOException`), or a missing directory (`DirectoryNotFoundException`). `GetLocalImagesEnabled()` is called inside `DoPreview`'s try block, so any of these fails the whole Markdown preview instead of just turning local images off. Fix: catch these errors too (or use `GetSettingsOrDefault`) and return `false`.

held.title: Raw-HTML rewrite only runs when the setting is ON and never strips srcset, unlike the description
held.body: The PR description says two things: - With the setting OFF, raw HTML `src` is rewritten to `#` so `data:` images cannot render. - `srcset` on raw `` is removed in both states. Here the whole rewrite sits inside `if (allowLocalImages)`, and nothing touches `srcset`. With the setting OFF, `` is left as is. In either state, `` keeps an unvalidated `srcset`. If `MarkdownPreviewHandlerControl.cs`, which I can't see, does not do this, the documented protections are missing. Fix: run the sanitizer in both states (rewrite everything to `#` when OFF) and remove `srcset` attributes.

held.title: The share-root calculation treats extended-length `\\?\` paths as UNC shares and widens the allowed base too far.
held.body: A path that starts with `\\` gets cut down to its first two components. For an extended-length path this gives the wrong base. `\\?\C:\Users\me\docs\a.md` becomes `\\?\C:`, which is the whole drive. `\\?\UNC\server\share\a.md` becomes `\\?\UNC`, which covers every server. With the second base, an image link like `\\?\UNC\attacker\share\p.png` passes the containment check. The handler then reads it over SMB, which is the tracking/credential-leak this feature is meant to prevent. I could not check whether Explorer ever passes `\\?\` or `\\.\` paths to the handler. Fix: normalise these prefixes first, or use `Path.GetPathRoot` on the full path to find the share root, and refuse local images when the root cannot be worked out.
